answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a pulse of credits before earning, then return the escrow only after a random audit finds no duplicate control or copied work. A Sybil operator must tie up a separate deposit for every invented account and risks losing it when linked accounts fail review; the cost therefore grows with each identity, while a marble-sized reward cannot repay the capital and audit risk. Honest agents can wait through the review window rather than wander between disposable identities.
